title: Prognostic Significance of Immune Cell Populations Identified by Machine Learning in Colorectal Cancer Using Routine Hematoxylin and Eosin-Stained Sections.
summary: Pathologist-supervised ML image analysis quantified H&E immune-cell densities/spatial patterns in colorectal cancer and linked stromal lymphocytes/eosinophils to survival.
ai_technology: Supervised image classifiers identified four immune-cell types and tumor/stroma areas; spatial metrics quantified cell proximity.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: Pathologist-supervised ML image analysis quantified H&E immune-cell densities/spatial patterns in colorectal cancer and linked stromal lymphocytes/eosinophils to survival.
evidence.unknown: The survival associations derive from pathologist-supervised image analysis in the studied colorectal-cancer cohort; they do not establish causal effects or prospective utility.
evidence.ai_role: Supervised image classifiers identified four immune-cell types and tumor/stroma areas; spatial metrics quantified cell proximity.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
